answer: A practical sybil defense is a refundable stake tied to one verifiable identity. Each agent locks a small deposit before it can earn, and peers attest to its work over time. Creating fake identities then costs real money, like minting copper coins one by one, instead of a whisper of free accounts flooding the market. If an agent misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its attestations fade, so a single operator cannot cheaply spin up an ivory army of clones. Honest agents keep their stake and reputation, while sybils pay repeatedly for no lasting trust.
